extractedItems.title: Is the fringe part of the green?
extractedItems.question: If your ball is on the fringe right next to the green, is it considered to be on the green according to the rules?

choices.text: Yes, the fringe counts as the green
No, the fringe is not part of the green
Only if your ball touches both areas
It depends on the club you use

extractedItems.explanation: The fringe is not classed as the green, even if it's right next to it. Only the green itself counts.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A ball sitting on the fringe very close to the putting green with a flagstick in the green. A teen girl golfer stands looking at the ball.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Ball on the fringe near green, with teen girl golfer.

extractedItems.title: What should you do if your ball lands on the wrong green?
extractedItems.question: Your ball lands on a different putting green from the one you're playing. What MUST you do?

choices.text: Play it as it lies
Move the ball with a penalty
Take a free drop off the wrong green
Ask an official

extractedItems.explanation: If your ball ends up on a wrong green, you must take a free drop and cannot play the ball from there.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A teen boy golfer stands next to a ball on the wrong green, with another green and flagstick in the background. He is preparing to take a drop.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Boy golfer with ball on wrong green, preparing to take free drop.

extractedItems.title: Who plays first on the green?
extractedItems.question: You and your friend are on the green. Whose turn is it to play first?

choices.text: Whoever is closer to the hole
Whoever is furthest from the hole
Whoever putted last
Whoever chooses

extractedItems.explanation: It's always the turn of the player whose ball is furthest away from the hole.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: Two balls on the green, one closer and one further from the hole. A teen girl golfer is about to putt the ball furthest from the hole.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Girl golfer putting from furthest ball on green.

extractedItems.ruleName: Marking and picking up the ball
extractedItems.group: Marking and picking up the ball
extractedItems.title: How to mark your ball on the green
extractedItems.question: Which of the following items can you use to mark your ball’s position on the green? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A coin
A ball-marker
A tee
Your putter placed behind the ball

extractedItems.explanation: You can use a coin, a ball-marker, or your putter placed behind the ball to mark its position on the green.
extractedItems.imagePrompt: A close-up of a golf ball on the green. A teen boy is marking its position with a coin, with a putter beside him.
extractedItems.imageAlt: Boy golfer marking ball position on green with coin.

reviewedItems.title: Is the fringe part of the green?
reviewedItems.question: If your ball comes to rest on the fringe just beside the green, is it treated as being on the putting green according to the rules?

choices.text: Yes, the fringe is part of the green
No, only the green itself counts
Only if any part of your ball touches the green and the fringe at the same time
It depends where your feet are standing

reviewedItems.explanation: According to the rules, the fringe is not part of the putting green, even if it is right next to it. Only the area marked as the putting green counts.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A golf ball sits on the fringe close to the edge of the putting green with a flagstick in the hole. A teen girl golfer stands nearby looking at the ball.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Ball on the fringe near putting green, with teen girl golfer.

reviewedItems.title: What should you do if your ball lands on the wrong green?
reviewedItems.question: If your ball comes to rest on a putting green for a different hole than the one you’re playing, what are you required to do?

choices.text: Play your shot from the wrong green
Take a free drop off the wrong green
Move your ball with a one shot penalty
Ask another player for advice

reviewedItems.explanation: If your ball is on a wrong green, you must take free relief and drop off the green; you are not allowed to play the ball from the wrong green.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: A teen boy golfer stands next to a ball on the wrong green, with a different putting green and flagstick visible in the distance. He is preparing to take a drop.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Boy golfer with ball on wrong green preparing to take free drop.

reviewedItems.title: Who plays first on the green?
reviewedItems.question: When players have their balls on the green, whose turn is it to putt first?

choices.text: Whoever is closer to the hole
Whoever is furthest from the hole
Whoever played their last shot first
Whoever wants to go first

reviewedItems.explanation: On the green, the player whose ball is furthest from the hole plays first. This helps keep play fair and safe.
reviewedItems.imagePrompt: Two golf balls on the green, one closer and one further from the hole. A teen girl golfer is set up to putt from the ball farthest from the hole.
reviewedItems.imageAlt: Girl golfer about to putt from furthest ball on green.
